config.title: useClickOutside

intro.title: useClickOutside
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom Vue composable called `useClickOutside` that detects when a user clicks outside a specific element on the page. You will learn how to use Vue's `ref` and `onMounted`/`onUnmounted` lifecycle hooks to manage DOM event listeners. The core programming concept involves handling click events and checking if the click target is outside a referenced element. By the end, you'll have a reusable composable that can enhance UI components like dropdowns or modals by closing them when a user clicks elsewhere.
intro.usecase: The useClickOutside pattern is essential for creating intuitive UI components that close or hide when users interact elsewhere on the page. You'll see this in production applications when closing dropdown menus after selecting an option, dismissing modal dialogs by clicking outside them, or collapsing search filters in e-commerce interfaces. As a Vue developer, implementing this pattern ensures your interactive elements behave predictably, improving user experience in admin dashboards, form wizards, and navigation systems. Mastering useClickOutside helps you build professional-grade components that respond naturally to user intent.

objectives: Construct a custom Vue composable function that detects clicks outside a specified element.
Initialize and manage reactive state to track the visibility of a target element.
Implement an event listener within the composable to capture click events on the document.
Apply conditional logic to hide the target element when a click occurs outside its boundaries.
Integrate the custom composable into a Vue component to control a dropdown or modal.
Bind the composable's reactive state to template directives for dynamic UI updates.
Configure the composable to properly clean up event listeners when the component unmounts.

successCriteria: The useClickOutside function includes document.addEventListener('click', handleClick) inside its body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're adding the event listener inside the useClickOutside function body.

steps.feedbackWrong: The cleanup function is missing or incorrect. Return a function that calls document.removeEventListener('click', handleClick).

steps.title: Create the modal structure
steps.instruction: In the App component's return object, add a template property that returns a div for the modal. Use v-if="isModalOpen" to conditionally render it and bind elementRef to the modal div using ref="elementRef".
steps.hint: The template should be a function that returns the modal structure. Remember to bind the ref to the modal div so useClickOutside can detect clicks outside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now returns a template with a modal div that conditionally renders based on isModalOpen and has elementRef bound to it.
successCriteria: The return object has a template property containing a modal div with v-if="isModalOpen" and ref="elementRef" attributes.
